harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 (7 compressed rotations via copytruncate + delaycompress), verified rotation behavior and continued writability both before and after a full node restart with changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: no active process holds app.log open, so copytruncate was chosen to guarantee uninterrupted writes regardless of the writer.
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app: daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate, create 0644 root root.

Validated config syntax with logrotate -d, then forced two rotation cycles with logrotate -f, confirming app.log stayed writable and rotated files appeared (app.log.1 plain, app.log.2.gz compressed per delaycompress).
Confirmed system logrotate.timer is enabled/active, so the config runs daily automatically.
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, config, log state).
Rebooted node1 via 'sudo -n reboot' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection.
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed (e8afb731... -> cb593cfa...), proving an actual restart.
Post-restart, verified logrotate config persisted, forced another rotation cycle, and confirmed app.log continued accepting writes after rotation (now at app.log.3.gz, 7-rotation retention intact).

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation of /var/log/inventory/app.log with 7 compressed rotations retained
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress; logrotate -d validated syntax and logrotate -f x2 produced app.log.1 (plain, delaycompress) then app.log.2.gz (compressed), confirming the rotation and retention scheme works.
copytruncate keeps app.log in place; after forced rotation, new writes ('post-rotation line', 'post-reboot write after rotation') landed in app.log successfully both pre- and post-restart.
systemctl is-active/is-enabled logrotate.timer shows active/enabled both before and after restart, so the daily cron-equivalent trigger is in place.
Captured boot_id e8afb731-420c-4162-a989-583aca271335, logrotate config, log directory state, and timer status prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledgement and disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo -n reboot' returned an immediate acknowledgement; the next exec call timed out, confirming the node went down for reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Polling succeeded once the node came back; boot_id changed to cb593cfa-a009-4b29-a057-aa58ab2f8e90, proving an actual reboot occurred (not just a service restart).

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: recovered state and data verified
evidence.summary: Post-restart, logrotate config file was intact, logrotate.timer was active/enabled, and a fresh forced rotation cycle correctly rotated files and preserved writability of app.log, confirming full functional recovery.
